mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the Taiwan incorporation agent and named signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the PRC investing parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (non-Hague route only): notarization before a PRC notary public -> PRC Provincial Foreign Affairs Office legalization -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification; two parallel legalization channels are never mixed.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all UBOs, directors, alternate directors, authorized signatories, shareholders with at least 25% ownership, and payment/collection counterparties against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, PRC foreign affairs sanctions list, Taiwan domestic jurisdictionally listed prohibited-party flags, and global PEP databases including family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is required for any name or address match, adverse media, sanctioned jurisdiction nexus, or high-risk payment activity related to Apple_IAP or Google_Play_Billing. Screening results must be retained for at least five years and re-run every 180 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Name and Business Scope Pre-check System / Company Registration Online System (Department of Commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Taiwan Company Act, the registered company name must be in traditional Chinese script and composed of a distinctive trade name followed by the business scope designation and the legal-form suffix 'Limited'. An English name may be recorded only as a secondary name for cross-border trade and must be a faithful transliteration or translation of the Chinese name if used on contracts or payment rails. The four-tier naming review examines: (1) absolute identity with an existing registered name; (2) identity of trade name with identical or similar business scope; (3) phonetic transliteration similarity likely to cause confusion; and (4) use of sensitive or regulated tokens that require prior ministerial consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the MOEA name pre-check is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the MOEA Department of Commerce within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching the original rejection decision, a revised list of up to five alternative names, and evidence that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to any pre-existing name. The appeal must also include prior ministerial approval for any sensitive token. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file a formal petition to the Executive Yuan within 30 days, followed by judicial review before the Taipei High Administrative Court, and may simultaneously reserve a revised new name through the online portal. Name reservation cannot be extended as a secret hold, but upon expiration a fresh pre-check application may be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For the proposed Taiwan-registered Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture operating an interactive audio chatroom and companion social app (ISIC 6311 / NAICS 519130), a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not inherently prohibited for company registration, provided a licensed corporate service provider maintains a physical Taiwan address where service of process and tax notices can be delivered. However, the National Taxation Bureau and AML-compliant banks will reject a bare virtual registered agent or commercial mailbox for this industry because the business has high digital cash flow, app-store settlement, user-generated content, and refunds that require operational substance, local books and records, principal staff at the physical location, and reconciliation of Apple_IAP and Google_Play_Billing flows. Therefore, virtual office is permissible only as an ancillary mail-forwarding point backed by a real office, local accountant, and server/payment-contract documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 35% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the National Taxation Bureau or MOEA-appointed registry officer during the first 12 months of operation. Inspection checklist: physical signage matching the registered name; presence of registered office and staff; board minutes and statutory books; employment or service-provider records; revenue and payment reconciliation reports; contracts with platform operators; UBO register access for competent authorities; power cords/server or cloud access evidence; and a properly maintained corporate chop/seal and bank correspondence. Failure to produce any of these items may trigger immediate fines, business closure, bank account suspension, or deemed loss of beneficial-owner transparency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 6, 129, 131, 148, 156, 172, 192, 203, 208, 216 and 218; Foreign Investment Act, Article 7; Regulations Governing the Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Chinese People, Articles 4 and 12; Business Registration Act, Article 6.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application and Certified Articles of Incorporation filed with the Department of Commerce, MOEA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the Taiwan Company Act, there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a company limited by shares. The JV must, however, subscribe paid-in capital at least equal to the amount approved by the Investment Commission, and the entire approved capital must be fully paid in cash at incorporation unless the Commission permits deferred payment. The remitted funds must be deposited in a newly opened temporary bank account in the name of the Company and certified by the bank before registration. The funds are not held in a blocked escrow account; after incorporation, control of the account passes to the board-authorized signatories. The paid-in capital should be commensurate with the registered business scope and working capital needs of the voice-streaming application; under the Foreign Investment Act, capital may be contributed in cash, machinery, technology or intellectual property, but for an ISIC 6311 service company cash contribution is recommended.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_JV_LTD (the 'Company'), adopted by the Board at a duly convened meeting at 10:00 a.m. on [Date] at the registered office in Taipei, Taiwan. Notice having been waived or given in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act, and a quorum of directors being present, the following resolutions were duly passed. RESOLVED, that the Company's Articles of Incorporation, as submitted to this Board and attached as Exhibit A, are hereby approved, adopted, and ratified in all respects, and that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [registered address] in Taipei, Taiwan, which address shall be stated in all corporate communications and filings with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the National Taxation Bureau, and all other competent authorities. RESOLVED, that the Board approves the subscription and issuance of the entire authorized share capital of the Company, consisting of [500,000] ordinary shares with par value NT$10 per share, aggregating NT$5,000,000 in paid-in capital, allocated among the JV shareholders in the proportions set forth in the Investment Commission approval letter; the funds shall be remitted to and held in a temporary corporate account until verified by the Company's bank. RESOLVED, that the Board authorizes the opening of banking accounts with [Bank Name] and designates the Chairperson and two additional directors as authorized signatories, such that any two signatures are required for disbursements above NT$500,000 and a single signature is sufficient for deposits and routine transactions below that threshold; the bank is irrevocably authorized to honor instruments bearing such signatures. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are elected and appointed effective immediately: [Name A], Chairperson; [Name B], Vice Chairperson; [Name C] and [Name D], Directors; and [Name E], Supervisor. The Chairperson is authorized to act as the legal representative, to execute all incorporation documents, to affix the company seal, to apply for the Unified Business Number, and to represent the Company before the Investment Commission, the Ministry of Economic Affairs, tax authorities, labor and health insurance administrations, and all other government offices. RESOLVED, that the Chairperson and any director are authorized to engage a registered corporate service agent or attorney, to pay all filing fees, and to take any further action lawfully required to complete incorporation and the opening of the Company's business operations, subject to the Foreign Investment Act and the Taiwan Company Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Commission Approval for Mainland China Investment and JV Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - Invest Taiwan online application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for pre-incorporation investment approval to the Investment Commission of Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs before making any company registry filing. The application must be filed through the online Invest Taiwan portal or delivered to the Investment Commission reception desk. Attach the JV agreement, a sworn declaration of mainland China investor identity, audited financial statements or bank reference of the mainland corporate shareholder, draft Articles of Incorporation, a five-year business plan, and a power of attorney appointing the local representative. The Commission will review the proposed shareholding ratio, capital amount, legal compliance, and national security impact. No capital may be remitted and no bank account may be opened until the approval letter is issued. If the Commission requests clarifications, respond within the stated cure period; an adverse decision may be appealed to the Executive Yuan.
required_dossiers: Completed investment application form
Joint venture agreement signed by all shareholders
Board resolution of the mainland China investor approving the investment
Five-year business plan for the voice-streaming application
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan local representative
Photocopies of passports or company registration certificates of shareholders
Audited financial statements or bank reference for the mainland corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission returns a query letter, the applicant has generally 14 days to file supplemental documentation through the same portal. If approval is denied, the investor may file administrative reconsideration with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of receipt, or submit a revised application with a reduced shareholding or narrower business scope.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Temporary Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: One-Stop Company Registration Portal, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Commission approval, apply for a company name reservation and business scope pre-check on the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal. The proposed English name must include Limited or Co., Ltd. and cannot duplicate an existing registered company. The application should describe the business scope as data processing, hosting and related activities; development of interactive audio and communication software; information service software; mobile application publishing; and voice-streaming social platform services. Once the name is reserved, open a temporary capital remittance account at a licensed bank and remit the approved paid-in capital from overseas. Obtain a Certificate of Deposit from the bank showing the Company name and amount. Name reservations are valid for six months and may be extended once.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Company name reservation application
Identification documents of the Taiwan representative
Bank remittance instruction and SWIFT copy
Certificate of Deposit issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to similarity, modify the name and file a new reservation; no fee is refunded for altered names. If the bank questions the source of remitted capital, provide the overseas remittance SWIFT reference, the underlying JV agreement, and a source-of-funds declaration from the remitting shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Founders' Meeting Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public within the jurisdiction of the Taiwan Taipei District Court; MOEA One-Stop Portal for template review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The shareholders must execute the notarized Articles of Incorporation and hold a founders' meeting. The articles must contain the corporate name, registered office address, business scope, authorized and issued share capital, classes of shares, mode of transfer, number of directors and supervisors, and method of election. Each shareholder's signature must be notarized by a Taiwan notary public, or by a Taiwan overseas representative office if executed outside Taiwan. At the founders' meeting, elect the first board of directors and the supervisor, and approve the issuance of shares in accordance with the capital subscribed. Prepare minutes certified by the meeting chairperson. The consolidated package, including the Investment Commission approval, must be delivered to the filing agent in preparation for submission to the Department of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the founders' meeting electing directors and supervisor
Investment Commission approval letter
Name approval certificate from MOEA
Shareholder consent letters and identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries the articles or minutes, correct the missing statutory clauses or signatures, re-execute the affected pages before the same notary, and redeliver within 15 days. If a shareholder refuses to sign, the majority shareholder may call an informal shareholders' meeting after notice, but formal incorporation should not proceed until the capital subscription schedule is amended and approved by the Investment Commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Filing and Certificate of Incorporation Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company registration application to the Department of Commerce, MOEA, through the one-stop registration system or in person at the central office in Taipei. The submission must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, founders' meeting minutes, Investment Commission approval, bank capital certificate, name reservation certificate, director and supervisor consent letters, and identification documents. Upon validation, the Department will issue the Company Registration Certificate and assign a Unified Business Number for profit-seeking enterprise tax purposes. The statutory processing target is up to seven working days if the documents are complete. After issuance, promptly file profit-seeking enterprise registration with the National Taxation Bureau and apply for company seal and stamp registration, because all subsequent licensing and employment filings require the Unified Business Number.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and founders' meeting minutes
Certificate of Deposit for paid-in capital
Investment Commission approval letter
Name reservation certificate
Director and supervisor acceptance letters
Identification documents and company seal card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Commerce suspends the application because of incomplete dossiers or inconsistency between the approved investment and the articles, the filing agent must remediate the discrepancy, obtain a revised Investment Commission approval if necessary, and resubmit within 30 days. If rejected, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days. The application can be accelerated using the one-stop expedited track once the requested corrections are made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Labor, Health Insurance, and Operating Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), Bureau of Labor Insurance (Ministry of Labor), National Health Insurance Administration, and licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate statutory post-incorporation registrations with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise registration and tax filing status, with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration for employees, and with the local municipal revenue service as required. The Company must also open the final corporate bank operating account at the bank named in the board resolution and deliver an original copy of the board resolution authorizing the signatories. Register the actual office premises with the local municipal government for business and municipal tax purposes; a lease agreement or ownership title must be on file. Since the activity is digital, no factory registration is triggered. Ensure that the voice-streaming platform's terms, data processing agreements, and privacy policies are in place before commercial launch.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Unified Business Number certificate
Tax registration application form
Bank account signatory resolution and specimen signatures
Lease agreement or title deed for the registered office
Appointment forms for labor insurance and national health insurance registration
Final board resolution for account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax, labor, or health registration is queried, provide the Unified Business Number and the required contracts or lease; late filings may incur penalties, so file a written explanation and pay any administrative fine before the bureau issues the registration. If the bank cannot complete final account activation, present the original certificate of incorporation and investment approval and reissue the board resolution with correct signatory names.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6311 interactive audio chatroom and companion social application is an information service activity; no factory, plant, assembly line, warehouse, chemical operation, or physical production facility is established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating license is triggered under Stage 2. The Company remains subject to general digital service, consumer protection, and personal data protection laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan - Not Applicable for ISIC 6311
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no environmental registration, no full EIA report, and no environmental license is required because the activity is purely digital and cloud-based; no physical plant, wastewater discharge, VOC emission source, or hazardous waste generation exists.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge points or stack emissions. If the Company later operates its own physical server rooms or data centers, energy efficiency and e-waste disposal standards under waste resource recycling regulations may apply, but they are outside the current Stage 2 scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure digital service. The Company's office premises must still comply with municipal building-code fire-safety reporting and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration requirements for general office work. If the Company operates its own on-site server room, a local fire inspection and Civil Defense permit may become necessary; for cloud-hosted voice-streaming applications, no physical fire permit is required under Stage 2.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance, including the competent National Taxation Bureau and its local tax office; electronic tax services are provided through the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal. Business registration and company or branch registration are administered through the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce and the relevant local authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Taiwan jurisdiction identifier in the payload is Taiwan, although the entity label Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is principally a PRC legal-form designation and is not a standard Taiwan company form. A Taiwan operating entity, branch, or subsidiary must first obtain the applicable foreign-investment approval and company, branch, or business registration through the Ministry of Economic Affairs and establish a Taiwan registered office. The entity then files its business registration and tax registration information with the competent National Taxation Bureau. The tax authority issues an eight-digit Unified Business Number, commonly used as the Taiwan business tax number and corporate tax identification number. VAT registration must be completed before commencing taxable business activities where registration is required. The registration package generally includes the approved company or branch registration documents, articles or constitutional documents, investment approval, responsible-person identification, registered-office evidence, bank-account information where requested, business scope, and power of attorney for an appointed tax agent or representative. Foreign entities without a Taiwan fixed place of business may be required to appoint a Taiwan tax agent or apply under the applicable rules for foreign electronic service providers. Separate platform, telecommunications, content, consumer-protection, personal-data, and payment compliance should be assessed because tax registration does not itself authorize operation of a voice-streaming social application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not generally provide a United States-style check-the-box election for classifying an incorporated company or branch. A Taiwan company is ordinarily subject to Taiwan corporate income tax on its taxable income, while a Taiwan branch of a foreign company is taxed under branch rules. A foreign company may be subject to Taiwan tax based on a Taiwan fixed place of business, agent, source income, or Taiwan-sourced electronic services. Taiwan has no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification mechanism that converts a limited company into a fiscally transparent entity. Treaty applications, withholding-tax relief, tax consolidation or filing-group treatment where legally available, and industry or investment incentives are relief or compliance mechanisms rather than entity-classification elections. Taiwan controlled foreign company rules and place-of-effective-management concepts may affect the tax treatment of offshore related entities, but they do not constitute a check-the-box election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added Tax under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Tax Act, principally administered through the National Taxation Bureau. Taiwan uses a business-tax system combining value-added tax and special non-value-added tax regimes; the ordinary regime is relevant to a Taiwan operating company providing digital application, subscription, advertising, virtual-item, or platform services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$480,000 of monthly sales is the principal small-business threshold commonly used for compulsory ordinary VAT registration analysis. This threshold does not remove the need for a company or business registration and does not necessarily determine registration obligations for foreign electronic service providers or businesses whose activities fall within mandatory registration rules. A Taiwan company or fixed-place business should register before commencing taxable transactions; foreign electronic service providers supplying Taiwan consumers may have separate registration obligations even without a Taiwan physical establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan electronic invoices are issued, transmitted, and reported through the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Platform or an approved service provider. Taxpayers must use the applicable electronic invoice format, assign a compliant invoice number, include the purchaser and transaction data required by the VAT rules, retain electronic records, and transmit the invoice data within the prescribed reporting period. Taiwan generally operates a post-issuance electronic reporting and platform-validation model rather than a universal real-time pre-clearance model for every transaction. B2B invoices ordinarily require the purchaser's Unified Business Number where applicable, while B2C invoices may use a carrier, mobile barcode, or donation code. The business must maintain API or approved-system controls for invoice issuance, cancellation, allowance notes, reconciliation, and audit retrieval. Apple App Store and Google Play billing require transaction-level analysis of the contractual seller, merchant of record, customer location, commission, remittance, invoice responsibility, and whether the Taiwan entity supplies the customer or merely receives platform settlement. Platform statements alone do not automatically establish export zero-rating or eliminate Taiwan VAT obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Taiwan VAT zero-rating may apply to qualifying exports of goods and to qualifying services supplied to foreign purchasers or connected with exports, subject to the statutory conditions and documentary evidence. For a voice-streaming or social application, zero-rating is not automatic merely because the customer uses an overseas payment card, because Apple or Google remits funds from abroad, or because the application is hosted outside Taiwan. The taxpayer should establish that the contractual customer is outside Taiwan, the service is supplied to and used by the foreign customer or otherwise falls within a statutory zero-rated category, the Taiwan entity is the actual supplier, consideration is received through permitted channels, and the transaction is recorded in the accounting and VAT systems. Services consumed by Taiwan users, Taiwan-resident subscribers, or Taiwan business customers generally require Taiwan VAT treatment even if payment is processed offshore. Exported goods require customs export evidence. Export-related services and offshore digital services require contracts, customer-residency evidence, service-delivery records, platform settlement reports, foreign-exchange or payment evidence, and a transaction-level allocation between Taiwan and non-Taiwan users. Input VAT refunds are generally available for qualifying zero-rated exporters to the extent permitted by the VAT rules, but refund claims remain subject to documentary and substantive verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and customs release evidence for exported goods; not applicable to a pure digital service unless physical goods are also exported
Commercial invoice, sales contract, purchase order, or equivalent evidence identifying the foreign purchaser and the exported goods or services
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier export record, or other transport evidence for physical goods, where applicable
Evidence of foreign purchaser location, including customer master data, contractual address, business registration, tax residence, and platform account records
For digital or offshore services, service agreement, order records, access or delivery logs, user-location evidence, platform merchant-of-record documentation, and settlement statements
Bank remittance advice, foreign-exchange receipt, or other permitted payment evidence linking the consideration to the claimed zero-rated transaction
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank-issued foreign-exchange evidence where required by the competent tax authority or used to substantiate foreign-currency proceeds
VAT sales ledger, electronic invoices or export documentation, credit notes, refund calculations, and reconciliation to general ledger and bank records

For Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, platform tax reports, merchant-of-record terms, gross customer billings, refunds, commissions, withholding, net remittances, and evidence identifying the supplier and customer jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The 180-day control period should be applied to export-proceeds monitoring where the relevant foreign-exchange or trade-control rule requires receipt or reporting within that period; Taiwan does not impose a universal tax rule that automatically makes every offshore digital-service receipt subject to a single 180-day repatriation deadline. Failure to support zero-rating may result in reassessment of output VAT at the applicable rate, denial or clawback of input-VAT refunds, interest, late-payment charges, and administrative penalties for inaccurate, omitted, or late VAT filings. False invoices, fabricated export documents, sham foreign customers, concealed Taiwan consumption, or intentional misrepresentation may trigger aggravated tax penalties and, depending on the conduct, criminal liability under tax, customs, commercial, foreign-exchange, or criminal laws. The tax authority may audit platform contracts, IP and device-location indicators, subscriber records, app-store reports, payment-processor data, bank remittances, related-party arrangements, and user-level allocation methodologies. A claim should therefore be reversed or amended promptly when export conditions fail, with a complete audit trail documenting the correction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), with foreign-exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Control Act and related CBC regulations. The Financial Supervisory Commission regulates banks, payment institutions, electronic payment institutions, and financial consumer protection. The Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission administers applicable inbound, outbound, and Mainland Area investment approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for current-account transactions, including bona fide trade in goods and services, subject to bank documentary review, reporting, and applicable anti-money-laundering controls. Capital-account transactions are more regulated. Inbound foreign investment, Mainland Area investment, equity transfers, shareholder loans, guarantees, and certain cross-border securities or intercompany financing may require prior approval, registration, reporting, or supporting documentation. A China-linked shareholder or investor requires separate analysis under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, related regulations, and Investment Commission practice. Profit remittance is generally feasible after corporate tax, withholding tax, accounting, statutory reserve, corporate approvals, and any required investment registration or approval are completed. Dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, and repayment of shareholder loans must be supported by the relevant contracts, board or shareholder resolutions, tax filings, withholding evidence, transfer-pricing support, and proof of available distributable funds. The proposed entity classification as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is not a standard Taiwan corporate form and must be reconciled with the actual place of incorporation, shareholder nationality, investment approval status, and applicable cross-Strait restrictions before banking or remittance implementation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not generally impose a universal mandatory foreign-exchange surrender ratio requiring all export proceeds to be converted into New Taiwan dollars. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to applicable bank reporting, documentary verification, accounting, tax, customs, and anti-money-laundering requirements. There is no generally applicable statutory rule requiring conversion of all export proceeds within a fixed number of days. Banks may require export declarations, commercial invoices, bills of lading, contracts, payment records, and evidence of the underlying transaction. Any specific industry, special-zone, subsidized-financing, customs, or investment approval condition must be checked separately. If the operating entity is actually established in Mainland China rather than Taiwan, Mainland China foreign-exchange rules apply instead, including SAFE registration, designated foreign-exchange bank review, and potentially different rules for export proceeds, capital contributions, and profit remittance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to Low for core treasury, payroll, local collections, and regulated payment activity. Taiwan does not provide an EU-style passport for offshore electronic-money institutions. An offshore digital EMI may provide corporate payment services only within the scope of its home-country authorization and the bank or correspondent-bank risk policy. It should not accept Taiwan deposits, operate a Taiwan payment account, provide Taiwan-regulated electronic payment services, or conduct local customer funds flows without the required Taiwan authorization or a licensed local partner. Offshore accounts do not replace a Taiwan corporate bank account for capital injection, tax payments, payroll, local vendor settlement, or regulated payment collection. Apple App Store and Google Play settlement should be mapped separately to the merchant-of-record, contractual recipient, withholding-tax position, foreign-exchange reporting, and Taiwan consumer-protection requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Taiwan banks commonly require original or certified corporate documents, beneficial-owner identification, authority evidence, specimen signatures, business-model explanations, and an interview with authorized representatives. Physical attendance is not universally mandated by statute, but banks may require in-person attendance where the ownership chain is foreign or China-linked, the business is a platform or digital-content business, the entity has no operating history, the source of funds is complex, or enhanced due diligence is triggered. Remote onboarding may be accepted selectively for low-risk cases or through an existing institutional relationship, subject to bank policy, notarization, legalization, video identification, and verification of signatory authority. A Mainland China shareholder, nominee structure, unexplained Taiwan connection, or high-volume cross-border payment model materially reduces the likelihood of fully remote onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear legal identity or mismatch between the stated Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture form and the actual Taiwan incorporation or registration status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation or registration, articles of incorporation, shareholder register, organizational chart, directors and officers register, legal opinion confirming the entity form, business registration, tax registration, and written explanation reconciling the China-Taiwan composite identifier with the actual operating jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: China-linked ownership, control, funding, or management that may implicate Taiwan cross-Strait investment restrictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ultimate-beneficial-owner chart, nationality and residency evidence, shareholder and control agreements, Investment Commission approval or confirmation of non-applicability, source-of-funds evidence, sanctions screening, related-party register, and legal memorandum addressing the Act Governing Relations between the Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Voice-streaming, social, user-generated-content, or platform activity presenting elevated content, consumer-protection, data, or payments risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product memorandum, customer and user geography, content-moderation policy, prohibited-content controls, age-verification procedures, terms of service, privacy policy, data-flow map, incident-response plan, platform contracts, payment-flow chart, and regulatory analysis confirming whether telecommunications, broadcasting, digital-platform, gambling, payment, or other sector licensing applies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of operating history, revenue evidence, or credible explanation for projected high transaction volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model, board-approved budget, signed commercial contracts, platform and app-store agreements, expected monthly transaction profile, customer and vendor geography, pricing schedule, invoices, bank statements, capitalization table, and management biographies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding, shareholder loans, unexplained intercompany transfers, or circular cash movements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan or investment agreements, board and shareholder resolutions, bank-origin evidence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds records, transfer-pricing analysis, intercompany-services agreements, beneficial-owner declarations, and a transaction-level funds-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore digital payment institutions, virtual-asset providers, payment aggregators, or accounts unrelated to the legal contracting entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licenses, compliance certificates, account ownership evidence, merchant-of-record agreements, settlement reports, processor due-diligence package, reconciliation controls, wallet or virtual-asset exclusion policy, and legal confirmation that the arrangement does not constitute unauthorized Taiwan payment or deposit-taking activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, politically exposed persons, opaque nominee shareholders, or adverse media involving founders or counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent identity verification, certified corporate records, beneficial-owner declarations, sanctions and PEP screening reports, adverse-media analysis, enhanced source-of-wealth evidence, litigation disclosures, and documented escalation and monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent foreign-exchange conversions without clear trade, service, investment, or treasury purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy, approved FX limits, underlying contracts, invoices, tax treatment, transaction-purpose coding, hedge documentation, forecast versus actual analysis, authorized-dealer correspondence, and monthly management information reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a Taiwan-authorized bank and remit from an account held in the registered investor's legal name. Before funding, complete all applicable Investment Commission, company-registration, capital-verification, and cross-Strait approvals or filings. The remittance instruction should identify the transaction as paid-in capital, capital increase, shareholder loan, or another legally accurate purpose; it must not describe debt as equity or use a generic personal remitter. Provide the bank with the investment approval or registration, subscription or investment agreement, board and shareholder resolutions, capitalization table, source-of-funds evidence, remitter ownership evidence, and beneficiary account details. The receiving bank should confirm the applicable foreign-exchange declaration, account classification, capital verification, and reporting process before receipt. Retain SWIFT payment messages, bank advice, foreign-exchange declarations, capital-account records, auditor or accountant certificates, and corporate registration evidence. Do not route paid-in capital through employee, director, unrelated affiliate, personal, virtual-asset, or unlicensed payment accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary services, software, hosting, advertising, professional fees, and platform costs, use bank transfers supported by contracts, invoices, tax withholding analysis, and evidence of service performance. SWIFT MT103 or its successor ISO 20022 payment message is suitable for standard cross-border wire settlement through an authorized bank; payment purpose, ordering customer, beneficiary, ultimate beneficiary, invoice reference, and fee allocation should be accurate. For goods or higher-risk counterparties, use a commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or controlled open-account process. A commercial LC should specify applicant, beneficiary, amount, currency, expiry, shipment or service documents, Incoterms where relevant, inspection requirements, sanctions clauses, discrepancy procedures, and applicable rules such as UCP 600 or ISP98 where appropriate. Outbound dividends, royalties, interest, management fees, and shareholder-loan repayments require separate tax, corporate-law, transfer-pricing, beneficial-owner, and foreign-exchange review and should not be disguised as trade payments. Maintain payment approval matrices, dual authorization, beneficiary screening, invoice matching, sanctions screening, and post-payment reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Taiwan-authorized bank, supported by documented forecast or existing foreign-currency exposure and entered into under the bank's master agreement and suitability procedures.

Currency swaps or foreign-exchange swaps with an authorized bank for documented liquidity, funding, or currency-mismatch management, subject to counterparty limits, valuation, collateral, accounting, and board-approved treasury policies.

Plain-vanilla currency options or option-based structures may be available from authorized banks, but require enhanced suitability review, risk disclosure, valuation controls, and evidence that the structure is a genuine hedge rather than speculative trading.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available through offshore or authorized counterparties for currencies where physical delivery is restricted, but availability, enforceability, reporting, tax, counterparty, and Taiwan foreign-exchange-control implications must be confirmed before execution. NDFs must not be used to evade Taiwan reporting, settlement, or capital-control requirements.

Hedging should be limited to identifiable operating, investment, financing, or forecast exposures; maintain hedge designations, notional limits, maturity matching, counterparty limits, independent valuation, cash-collateral controls, and accounting documentation. Speculative leveraged derivatives, unsupported rolling positions, and transactions with unlicensed providers should be prohibited.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory headline Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax (PSEIT) rate of 20% on taxable net income. No general tax holiday applies to interactive audio chatroom applications, but the Basic Taxation Act applies an alternative minimum tax of 12% where effectively taxable income exceeds NT$20 million. Qualifying research and development expenditures may earn investment tax credits under the Industrial Innovation Act. A 5% retained-earnings surtax applies to unappropriated earnings distributed after statutory allowance. No special preferential regime for app-store revenues is available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (Form 15); filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance tax e-Filing system (Combination of Electronic Reporting and Electronic Payment Platform).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, no later than 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from voice streaming subscription fees, in-app virtual gifts, and other digital content sales generated in Taiwan.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Taiwan-source gross revenue even if collected through Apple App Store or Google Play. App-store commissions and payment-processing fees are deductible as operating costs only when properly documented in tax books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of producing services: hosting and bandwidth, content licensing, payment processing fees, and platform distribution commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to non-resident licensors are subject to 20% withholding tax and should be recorded net of withholding; attach withholding certificate Form 20A and tax payment vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, staff remuneration, rent, administrative overhead, depreciation, and amortisation attributable to the Taiwan operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service fees paid to foreign cloud or marketing providers are taxable Taiwan-source income where services are effectively used in Taiwan; ensure the foreign vendor is unable to obtain treaty relief and that withholding is reported under Article 88.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains, and other non-business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid by related non-resident lenders is subject to 20% withholding tax; thin capitalisation rules may disallow interest deductions exceeding a 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign exchange losses, impairment losses, and non-business expense items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related party service fees must be substantiated with contracts, invoices, and proof of actual service performance; otherwise deductions will be denied and the payment treated as a constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back items such as exempt gains, tax-exempt income, and other adjustments required under the Basic Taxation Act (Income Basic Tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to foreign shareholders unless the Taiwan entity is an investment-structured captive engaged in tax-shielding transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income computed after statutory deductions, loss carryforward, and all adjustment entries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan-resident JV must use arm's length intercompany transfers; any deviation is recorded here as a disallowed expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount produced by applying the 20% statutory rate to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available for taxes paid in China or other countries on income that is also subject to Taiwan tax, limited to the Taiwan tax attributable to such income and evidenced by Tax Residence Certificate and tax payment proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 5% surtax computed on unappropriated earnings where profits are not distributed to shareholders before the deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PRC parent controls distribution policy, the JV must document that unappropriated earnings are accumulated for legitimate business expansion; otherwise the 5% surtax plus penalties will be imposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after credits and provisional prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-residents are treated as repatriation if disguised as deductible expenses; maintain clear supporting documentation for all cross-border payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing results in a surcharge of 1% of the unpaid tax for each month of delay, up to 20% of the tax due. If no tax is payable, a fixed late-filing fine between NT$1,500 and NT$15,000 is imposed. Understatement attributable to concealment or false reporting triggers a penalty of 1 to 2 times the understated tax (or 2 to 3 times for repeated violations), plus interest at legal rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% for dividends paid to a non-resident enterprise; 21% for dividends paid to a non-resident individual. For a Mainland China parent or shareholder, the 20% statutory rate currently applies because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement signed in 2015 has not entered into effect; no reduced dividend rate is available without an effective treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a bilateral tax treaty exemption or reduced rate, the withholding agent must, before making the payment, submit to the National Taxation Bureau: (a) a completed Application for Reduced Withholding Tax Rate (Form 20A for non-resident enterprises), (b) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction's competent authority that resides in the tax year of payment, (c) evidence of beneficial ownership, and (d) the relevant underlying contract. The Taiwan tax authority generally issues a written approval within 30 days. Without an effective TRC, the standard 20% / 21% rates apply. China currently lacks a fully effective cross-strait tax agreement, so treaty relief for PRC investors is not administratively available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates are 20% on royalties and 20% on interest paid to non-resident enterprises; interest on short-term commercial paper is withheld at 15%. Under Taiwan's effective comprehensive tax treaties, royalty and interest rates are frequently reduced to 10%. No treaty relief exists for Mainland China payments because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement is not legislatively implemented; therefore a 20% withholding cost remains for Pakistan licence fees or debt interest paid to PRC related parties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Taiwan resident company must prepare a Transfer Pricing Report (Local File) when the total amount of related-party transactions exceeds NT$200 million (approximately USD 6.6 million). A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required when the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent enterprise reaches NT$27 billion (approximately EUR 750 million). A simplified local file may be required when cross-border related-party transactions exceed NT$50 million or domestic related-party transactions exceed NT$100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not enact Gulf-style annual Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Nevertheless, the Income Basic Tax Act and the Income Tax Act Article 43-1 authorise tax authorities to disregard transactions or legal forms that lack economic substance, including interposing shell companies and allocating income to tax haven entities. Thin capitalisation rules limit interest deductions to a debt-to-equity ratio of 3:1. Treaty benefits and cross-strait relief are denied to entities without actual management, employees, office space, and business activities in Taiwan. For a voice streaming joint venture, the entity must demonstrate substantive operational substance covering: Taiwan-based product management, customer transaction review, app store servicing, technical hosting arrangements, and local decision-making records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting in-app voice stream purchases, virtual gifts, and subscription revenue; failure to issue VAT unified invoices for Taiwan sales; routing customer revenue into personal bank accounts or offshore e-wallets controlled by the parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act Article 110, a taxpayer filing an understated return is liable for a fine equal to the amount of tax understated, and up to twice the understated tax when concealment or intentional misstatement is established. Under the Tax Collection Act Article 41, intentional tax evasion by fraudulent means leads to imprisonment of not more than 5 years, short-term imprisonment, or a fine of up to NT$1,000,000, plus the evaded tax and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director can be held jointly liable for the delinquent tax where the company fails to pay; under Tax Collection Act Article 24, the director's departure from Taiwan may be restricted when tax arrears are material. Criminal imprisonment for intentional evasion attaches to the actual responsible person, and a civil court may pierce the corporate veil where the director concealed revenue for personal benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing non-arm's-length royalty, service, or management fees with the PRC parent or affiliated app developers; setting an artificially low gross margin in Taiwan while placing high-margin functional returns in a low-tax affiliate; failing to maintain contemporaneous Local File documentation after related-party transactions exceed NT$200 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will adjust related-party income under Income Tax Act Article 43-1 and may recharacterise the arrangement, resulting in additional corporate income tax, a 1% monthly late surcharge up to 20%, and an understatement penalty of up to twice the tax deficiency. Failure to supply TP documentation after an official request may result in a penalty of NT$1,000 to NT$10,000 per item and additional adjustments for intentional non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the adjusted tax remains unpaid, directors of the Taiwan JV may face collection against personal assets under Tax Collection Act Article 23 and 24-regime including bank levies and travel bans. A director who knowingly constructs artificial transfer prices is criminally liable under tax evasion provisions if the adjustment is classified as intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Substance Abuse and AML Offences
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Taiwan entity as a brass-plate or conduit with no real employees, no board minutes, no office lease, or no substantive decision-making; transferring app-store proceeds immediately to the PRC parent; failing to conduct anti-money-laundering risk assessment and regulatory filings for inbound app revenue streams; failing to maintain transaction records for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The jurisdictional tax authority may deny treaty benefits and recharacterise the entity's income as earned by the parent; fictitious deductions are reversed. Under the Money Laundering Control Act, enterprises that fail to establish AML internal controls risk administrative fines of up to NT$5,000,000 and responsible persons are subject to up to 2 years imprisonment if the omission is conducted with wilful negligence. The Central Bank and Financial Supervisory Commission may freeze suspicious account traffic.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who use the Taiwan JV as a shell to launder subscriber payments or evade taxes are individually accountable for AML violations; corporate veil-piercing can expose personal assets. Taiwanese courts have upheld travel restrictions and asset seizure against responsible persons where the entity operates without real substance and the director's personal conduct enables the abuse.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mischaracterising dividend repatriation as tax-deductible management fees, royalty payments, intercompany loans, or service fees to avoid the 20% dividend withholding tax; omitting withholding tax and remittance filings on payments to foreign payees; structuring loan agreements without genuine expectation of repayment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act Article 114, a withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit is liable for the full unpaid tax amount plus a fine of 1 to 3 times the amount improperly shipped. The transaction may be reclassified as a dividend and subject to the 20% withholding tax, the 5% retained-earnings surtax, and interest. Criminal liability under Tax Collection Act Article 42 can reach 3 years' imprisonment for willful failure to withhold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the withholding agent are personally responsible for unpaid withholding tax when they have signed or directed the payments. Civil restitution may be ordered from directors to recover unlawful distributions; travel bans and passport revocation may be requested by the National Taxation Bureau for unremitted withholding obligations above material amounts, and repeated deliberate conduct exposes the responsible person to criminal imprisonment.
